policy_title: Independent Review for a Genuine Living Wage
stated: Establish an independent review to recommend a genuine living wage across all sectors, with government departments and all other public sector employers taking a leading role in paying it.

source.quote: Establish an independent review to recommend a genuine living wage across all sectors, with government departments and all other public sector employers taking a leading role in paying it.

bearing_set.reason: Directly targets pay levels for low-paid workers by recommending a 'genuine living wage' (higher than the statutory floor) and mandating public sector employers to lead on paying it — a clear, non-negligible verdict on fair pay and job quality.

A genuine living wage is explicitly designed to bring wages up to the cost of essentials; raising pay floors for lower-income workers has a direct, material effect on real disposable income and ability to afford food, energy and bills.

A living wage by design lifts the bottom of the wage distribution; to the extent it is adopted, it narrows the gap between lower-paid and higher-paid workers, directly moving income inequality indicators.

The explicit commitment that government departments and public sector employers pay the recommended rate increases the public-sector wage bill; mechanism is direct (higher payroll expenditure → funded-vs-borrowed pressure), and the indicator — sustainability of the spending path — is concrete even if the magnitude depends on the review's outcome.

membership_note: Policy bears most heavily on O4 (its designed purpose) and O14 (distributional narrowing effect); O12 is included because the public-sector employer commitment is a direct fiscal undertaking with a traceable mechanism, not a vague 'it costs money' assertion.
